Question: A point \(P\) lies in the same plane as a given square of side \(1.\) Let the vertices of the square, taken counterclockwise, be \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D.\) Also, let the distances from \(P\) to \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C,\) respectively, be \(u,\) \(v\) and \(w.\) What is the greatest distance that \(P\) can be from \(D\) if \(u^2+v^2=w^2?\)
